req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET / returns HTTP 200 with HTML listing all posts ordered by created DESC. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — normal GET / with pre-loaded fixture data returns 200 and contains the known post title; (2) negative NEG — verifying that a non-existent route returns 404, not 200, confirming the status-code check is meaningful; (3) boundary BVA — empty database (no posts) still returns 200 with valid HTML but no post titles; (4) DT — multiple posts are ordered newest-first (DESC), catching ORDER BY direction mutations; (5) STC — unauthenticated vs authenticated client both see the index at 200, confirming no login gate on GET /.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_and_contains_fixture_post_title
preconditions: Database initialised with fixture data (1 post: 'test title' by user 'test')
actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
trace: R-FLASKR-001: HTTP 200; HTML with post titles
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_returns_200_and_contains_fixture_post_title():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'text/html' in r.content_type.encode()
    assert b'test title' in r.data

import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    from flaskr.db import get_db
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_with_empty_database_returns_200_no_posts():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' not in r.data
    assert len(r.data) > 0

tests.name: test_index_posts_ordered_newest_first
preconditions: A second post with a later created timestamp is inserted
actions: Insert a newer post with title 'newer post title'
Send GET / with the Flask test client
expected: b'newer post title' appears before b'test title' in the response body
Both post titles are present in the response
trace: R-FLASKR-001: posts ordered by created DESC — catches ORDER BY ASC mutation
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    from flaskr.db import get_db
    db = get_db()
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        ('newer post title', 'body2', 1, '2025-06-01 12:00:00')
    )
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_posts_ordered_newest_first():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.data
    assert b'newer post title' in body
    assert b'test title' in body
    idx_newer = body.find(b'newer post title')
    idx_older = body.find(b'test title')
    assert idx_newer < idx_older

actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
expected: Response body contains opening HTML tag

from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_response_content_type_is_html():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.content_type.startswith('text/html')
    assert b'<html' in r.data.lower() or b'<!doctype' in r.data.lower()
    assert b'test title' in r.data
